<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
## Problem

Custom `.agent.md` files now support the `reasoning-effort` frontmatter property:

```yaml
---
name: Code-Review
model: GPT-5.6 Sol (copilot)
reasoning-effort: xhigh
---
```

However, the behavior currently differs depending on which harness executes the custom agent.

The Copilot Agent Host path forwards `reasoning-effort` to the Copilot SDK as `CustomAgentConfig.reasoningEffort`, as implemented in #329263.

The local VS Code chat harness does not appear to preserve or apply the same custom-agent reasoning-effort value.

In the local harness, `ICustomAgent` currently contains fields such as `model`, `tools`, and agent instructions, but not the configured reasoning effort. When `runSubagent` creates the child request, its `modelConfiguration` is resolved from the selected model configuration instead:

```ts
modelConfiguration: modeModelId
    ? this.languageModelsService.getModelConfiguration(modeModelId)
    : undefined,
```

As a result, the reasoning effort selected in the model picker / parent session is used even when the invoked custom agent explicitly declares a different `reasoning-effort`.

## Example

Given:

```yaml
# Code-Review.agent.md
---
name: Code-Review
model: GPT-5.6 Sol (copilot)
reasoning-effort: xhigh
---
```

and a parent session using:

```text
GPT-5.6 Sol
Reasoning effort: high
```

invoking `Code-Review` through the local `runSubagent` path currently results in the subagent running with:

```text
reasoning effort: high
```

rather than the expected:

```text
reasoning effort: xhigh
```

The same `.agent.md` property is honored by the Copilot Agent Host path.

## Expected behavior

`reasoning-effort` should have consistent semantics across custom-agent execution paths.

For both direct custom-agent execution and local `runSubagent` invocation:

1. If the custom agent declares a supported `reasoning-effort`, use that value.
2. If the custom agent does not declare one, inherit the current model/session configuration as today.
3. If a future explicit per-invocation reasoning-effort override is added to `runSubagent`, that explicit value should take precedence over the custom-agent default.

A reasonable precedence order would be:

```text
explicit per-invocation override
    >
custom .agent.md reasoning-effort
    >
picker / parent model configuration
    >
model default
```

## Suggested implementation

The local custom-agent representation could retain the parsed reasoning-effort value, for example:

```ts
export interface ICustomAgent {
    // ...
    readonly model?: readonly string[];
    readonly reasoningEffort?: string;
    // ...
}
```

Then, when constructing the child request, the local harness could merge the agent-specific effort into the resolved model configuration:

```ts
const modelConfiguration = modeModelId
    ? this.languageModelsService.getModelConfiguration(modeModelId)
    : undefined;

// Conceptually:
if (subagent?.reasoningEffort) {
    modelConfiguration.reasoningEffort = subagent.reasoningEffort;
}
```

The exact implementation can of course follow the existing model-configuration helpers and validation paths.

The same resolution should also be applied when a custom agent is selected directly from the agent picker, not only when it is invoked as a subagent.

## Why this matters

Currently, `reasoning-effort` is a supported `.agent.md` property, but whether it actually affects execution depends on the selected harness.

That makes shared custom agents difficult to reason about and can silently change latency, token usage, and behavior.

It is especially useful for multi-agent workflows where different roles intentionally use different reasoning budgets, for example:

```text
Explorer       -> medium
Implementation -> high
Code Review    -> xhigh
Planner        -> xhigh
```

These defaults should remain part of the agent definition regardless of whether the custom agent runs through the local VS Code harness or the Copilot Agent Host.

## Relationship to other issues

This is separate from #327099, which requests a dynamic reasoning-effort parameter on individual `runSubagent` invocations.

This issue is only about honoring the existing declarative `reasoning-effort` property from the target custom `.agent.md` file in the local harness.

Related:

* #313546 — Support reasoning effort configuration in custom `.agent.md` files
* #329263 — Support reasoning effort in custom agent files
* #327099 — Allow specifying reasoning effort per subagent invocation
issues.title: Local harness should honor `reasoning-effort` from custom `.agent.md` files

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
### Problem

Extensions that implement a modal or chorded input layer (vscode-neovim, VSCodeVim,
Emacs emulations) resolve keys inside their own runtime. VS Code has no knowledge
that these bindings exist, so the Command Palette, menu items, and hover tooltips
always show the default binding, even when it is not what the user would press.

Example: with vscode-neovim, `workbench.action.quickOpen` is reachable via a
user-defined Neovim mapping (`<leader>ff`). The Command Palette shows `Ctrl+P`.
The displayed hint is not wrong, but it is not the binding the user actually uses,
and the real one is undiscoverable through the UI.

These bindings cannot be declared in `package.json` because they are defined by the
user at runtime, in the extension's own configuration format, and can change without
a reload.

### Proposed API

A display-only registration, with no effect on dispatch:

    vscode.keybindings.registerHint(commandId, {
      label: "space f f",
      when: "neovim.mode == 'normal'"
    })

VS Code would surface `label` wherever it currently renders a keybinding for that
command, when `when` evaluates true. Resolution and dispatch are untouched.

### Why existing mechanisms do not cover this

- `contributes.keybindings` is static and cannot express user-defined runtime mappings.
- Rebinding through `keybindings.json` is not viable: these are multi-key sequences
  with modal context, beyond what the two-chord resolver expresses.
- #196835 (read access to keybindings) was closed as not planned, and would not
  help here regardless, since the binding does not exist in VS Code's registry at all.

### Who benefits

Any extension with an internal input layer. The concrete case is modal editing
extensions, which have a large installed base and currently give users a UI that
reports bindings the user does not press.

Two things to expect: it may be closed as a duplicate of the broader dynamic-keybinding threads, and "display-only" is the load-bearing part of the pitch. If it reads as "let extensions own keybinding resolution", it gets closed immediately.

Sources:
- microsoft/vscode #196835
- microsoft/vscode #1422
- microsoft/vscode #111854
- VSpaceCode/vscode-which-key
- VSpaceCode which-key docs
issues.title: API for extensions to register display-only keybinding hints

## Feature request

Provide product-protocol URLs that can be opened from a browser or another application to focus the Agents window and reveal a specific Agent Host session or chat.

Proposed URL shapes:

- `vscode://agents/agent-host-session/<provider>/<session-id>`
- `vscode://agents/agent-host-session/<provider>/<session-id>?chat=<chat-id>`

## Motivation

The existing `agent-host-session://` links are internal workbench links. They are not registered with the operating system and therefore cannot be opened from a browser, issue, terminal output, or another application.

Using an Agents-specific product URL ensures the target opens in the Agents window rather than whichever VS Code window or compatible application happens to be active. The provider remains part of the URL because backend session IDs are provider-scoped.

Agent Host session and chat context menus should also provide a **Copy Link** action so users can share these browser-addressable URLs.

This complements #332186, which added internal deep links and rich session/chat pills.

1. In the Agents Window, open the context menu for an Agent Host session and choose **Copy Link**.
2. Paste the copied URL into a browser, terminal, or another external application and open it.
3. Verify VS Code focuses or opens the Agents Window and reveals the exact target session.
4. Open a session containing multiple chats, use **Copy Link** on a specific chat, and open that URL externally.
5. Verify the Agents Window opens the exact target chat, not only the session’s default or currently active chat.
6. Repeat while another VS Code window or session is active and verify the target still opens in the Agents Window.
7. Verify invalid, missing, or unknown provider/session/chat identifiers fail safely without opening an unrelated session.

issues.body:
## Feature request
Allow users to explicitly choose whether an agent-created independent session uses a new Git worktree. The `create_session` tool should honor that choice rather than relying only on inherited isolation.

Implemented by #335076.

## Expected behavior
- Set `worktree: true` only when the user explicitly requests a new worktree.
- Set `worktree: false` only when the user explicitly requests working without a worktree.
- Omit `worktree` when the user has not made an explicit choice, preserving existing isolation inheritance/defaults.
- Never combine `worktree` with `relationship: currentSession`; either boolean value is rejected before creating a chat or session.
- With `worktree: false`, resolve a known existing worktree folder to its project root before creating the independent session.

## Verification steps
Use the Agents window with a Git project and inspect the `create_session` tool arguments and the resulting working directory/branch, not just the assistant summary.

1. **Explicit worktree:** Ask “Start implementation in a new independent session with a new worktree.” Verify `relationship: independent`, `worktree: true`, and a newly created worktree.
2. **No worktree from an existing worktree:** Start from a session already using a managed worktree and ask “Start implementation in a new independent session without a worktree.” Verify `worktree: false`; the new session uses the known project root, not the parent worktree, and no additional worktree is created.
3. **No explicit choice:** Ask for an independent session without mentioning worktrees. Verify the agent omits `worktree`. For the same project, existing isolation is inherited; a different project retains the existing worktree default.
4. **Current-session work:** Ask for a new chat in the current session. Verify `relationship: currentSession`, no `worktree` argument, and the existing workspace is shared.
5. **Folder fallback:** Request an independent session without a worktree for a folder with no known project mapping. Verify that the supplied folder is used directly.
6. If available, repeat step 2 for a remote project and verify that its remote URI/authority is preserved.

Unit tests additionally cover invalid boolean values and rejection of `currentSession` combined with either `worktree: true` or `worktree: false`.
issues.title: Allow explicit worktree selection when agents create independent sessions

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Compare multiple implementation attempts in the Agents window

The Agents window supports multi-chat sessions, peer-chat forks, isolated worktrees, and reviewing changes beside a conversation. However, after exploring more than one approach, users must manually inspect each chat and diff to determine which implementation is better.

Add a **Compare Attempts** workflow that runs or selects multiple approaches to the same task and presents their outcomes in a code-oriented comparison.

## Proposed experience

Add a **Compare Agents** toggle to the new-session input alongside the existing harness and model controls.

- When the toggle is off, the current single-harness behavior is unchanged.
- When the toggle is on, the harness picker becomes multi-select and the send action indicates how many attempts will run, for example **Run 3 Attempts**.
- The model remains a single shared selection. Only harnesses that advertise that model are eligible; incompatible harnesses are disabled with an explanation.
- The prompt, workspace, starting branch or commit, permission level, and isolation configuration are shared across all attempts.

Submitting the prompt fans it out to one new session per selected harness. The sessions are placed in a comparison group so they can be tracked together, while a failure to start one harness does not discard successful attempts.

Each attempt:

- receives the same prompt and starts from the same repository state;
- runs in a separate session and isolated worktree;
- uses one selected harness and the shared model;
- remains independently reviewable and editable.

Once at least two attempts have results, VS Code offers a comparison view containing:

- a concise implementation summary for each attempt;
- changed files and diff size;
- test, build, lint, and diagnostic results;
- unresolved errors or warnings;
- elapsed time and usage;
- notable architectural or behavioral differences;
- overlapping, conflicting, and attempt-specific changes.

The user can then:

- **Use attempt A** or **Use attempt B**;
- open the diffs side by side;
- send feedback to one attempt;
- ask an agent to **Synthesize the best of both** into a new attempt;
- discard the unused worktrees.

## Why this belongs in the Agents window

This makes existing multi-session and worktree support useful as a deliberate workflow rather than just additional tabs. The Agents window can provide a stronger experience than a generic best-of-N response because it understands source control state, diagnostics, tests, diffs, and editor navigation.

It also gives users a concrete way to use parallel agents without introducing a separate multi-session dashboard.

## Related approaches

Cursor 2.2 introduced **multi-agent judging**, which evaluates parallel agent runs after they finish, recommends a solution, and explains the selection. This validates the need for a decision step on top of parallel execution. The VS Code opportunity is to make the underlying code evidence inspectable and support user-controlled synthesis rather than stopping at a winner recommendation.

- [Cursor changelog: Multi-agent judging](https://cursor.com/changelog/page/12)

OpenAI Codex has a **Best of N** feature that generates multiple responses for one task so users can explore alternatives and choose an approach. The Codex app also supports parallel agents in isolated worktrees and reviewing and commenting on each agent's diff.

This proposal is not a request for exact parity. VS Code can provide a more code-native comparison by combining its multi-chat sessions, worktrees, diff editors, diagnostics, test results, and usage data into one decision surface. The distinguishing workflow is comparing validated implementation outcomes, then selecting or synthesizing them without manually reconciling separate chats.

- [Codex changelog: Best of N](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11428266-codex-changelog)
- [Introducing the Codex app](https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-codex-app/)

## Suggested initial scope

An initial version could:

1. Add comparison mode to the new-session input.
2. Let the user select two or more compatible harnesses and one shared model.
3. Fan out the same request into a separate worktree-isolated session for each harness.
4. Keep the resulting sessions together as a comparison group.
5. Compare summaries, changed files, diff statistics, diagnostics, validation results, elapsed time, and usage.
6. Open the chosen attempt's diff and worktree.

Automatic synthesis, applying the winner, and worktree cleanup could follow later.

## Acceptance criteria

- One submission can launch two or more harness-specific sessions for comparison.
- VS Code clearly indicates whether their starting repository state differs.
- Validation results distinguish passed, failed, not run, and unknown.
- Selecting an attempt does not silently overwrite the user's current working tree.
- Unselected attempts remain available until the user explicitly discards them.
- The workflow is keyboard accessible and supports any selected harness that provides the shared model and isolated worktrees.
issues.title: Agents window: Compare multiple implementation attempts

issues.body:
## Problem

Agent Host currently supplies a static GitHub token when creating Copilot SDK sessions. Some GitHub tokens have a known finite lifetime, and the Copilot SDK supports a `gitHubTokenProvider` callback for refreshing those credentials.

Without carrying token lifetime to Agent Host and selecting the provider callback, a long-running Copilot session can continue using an expired token or surface an interactive authentication prompt instead of requesting a fresh credential.

## Desired behavior

- Carry optional OAuth-style `expiresIn` through Agent Host authentication and reconnect/replay.
- Deduct elapsed time when credentials are replayed and do not replay expired credentials.
- Use a static `gitHubToken` when expiry is unknown.
- Use `gitHubTokenProvider` when expiry is known, never both options at once.
- Coalesce concurrent SDK refresh callbacks and map refresh requests to the existing Agent Host authentication-required flow.
- Bound refresh waits so the SDK cannot wait indefinitely when no client supplies a replacement.
- Restart the Copilot client when switching between static and provider-backed credential modes.

## Implementation

Implemented by #334418, with unit coverage for credential selection, refresh coalescing, timeout behavior, replay, and mode transitions. The refresh path was also validated end to end with a real Microsoft-brokered GitHub token renewal.
issues.title: Agent Host: Support expiring GitHub tokens with the Copilot SDK

issues.body:
## Problem

The GitHub Authentication extension can broker GitHub access tokens through a signed-in Microsoft Entra account. These exchanged GitHub tokens have a finite lifetime, but the extension previously treated them like ordinary persisted GitHub OAuth tokens with no known expiry or renewal path.

Once an exchanged token expired, consumers could lose authentication and fall back to an interactive sign-in prompt even though the Microsoft account was still signed in and could silently mint a replacement.

## Desired behavior

- Keep the exchanged token's absolute expiry internally.
- Return its current relative lifetime through `AuthenticationSession.expiresIn`.
- Recompute the remaining lifetime whenever a cached session is returned.
- Silently renew Microsoft-brokered GitHub sessions before expiry, including the one-hour threshold required by the Copilot SDK.
- Coalesce concurrent renewal attempts.
- Retain a still-valid token when proactive renewal fails transiently, and only remove the session after the token actually expires.
- Leave ordinary persisted GitHub OAuth sessions unchanged when their expiry is unknown.

## Implementation

Implemented by #334418, including mocked coverage for initial exchange, restore, cached lifetime recomputation, renewal, and transient renewal failures.
issues.title: GitHub Authentication: Support expiring GitHub tokens brokered through Microsoft Entra

issues.body:
## Problem

`AuthenticationSession` exposes an access token but not its lifetime. Consumers that integrate with SDKs supporting renewable credentials cannot tell whether a token is static or when it should be refreshed.

#152517 previously proposed exposing an absolute `expiresAt` timestamp. An absolute timestamp is unsafe across VS Code's client/remote extension-host boundary because the two machines may have clock skew.

## Proposed API

```ts
export interface AuthenticationSession {
	/**
	 * The access token's remaining lifetime, in seconds, when the authentication provider returns the session.
	 *
	 * This corresponds to `expires_in` in an OAuth 2.0 token response. Providers returning
	 * cached sessions must recompute this value. This is undefined when the authentication
	 * provider does not know the access token's expiry. When defined, this must be a positive integer.
	 */
	readonly expiresIn?: number;
}
```

## Semantics

- The value is a positive integer representing whole seconds remaining when the session is returned.
- Cached sessions recompute the value on every return.
- `undefined` means the provider does not know the token's expiry.
- The relative lifetime avoids comparing clocks across extension-host boundaries.

## Implementation

The proposed declaration and first consumer are implemented experimentally in #334418 under `vscode.proposed.authSessionExpiration.d.ts`.

Related to #152517.
issues.title: API proposal: Expose AuthenticationSession access token lifetime

issues.body:
When `"chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled": true` and a local folder contains a supported `devcontainer.json`, the Agents workspace picker should expose Dev Container execution directly from that folder row.

## Proposed behavior

- Show a side-chevron submenu on eligible local folder rows.
- Include a **Use Dev Container** action in the submenu.
- Selecting the action should create the draft using the existing Dev Container Agent Host flow.
- Update the selected workspace label to `<folder name> - Dev Container`.
- Keep the action keyboard accessible and expose the selected label to screen readers.
- Do not show the submenu when the setting is disabled, the folder lacks a supported Dev Container configuration, Docker is unavailable, or the workspace is not local.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Eligible local folder rows display the submenu affordance.
2. Choosing **Use Dev Container** preserves the selected folder and enables Dev Container execution for the draft.
3. The workspace picker trigger reads `<folder name> - Dev Container` after selection.
4. Normal folder selection continues to use the local workspace flow.
5. Focused unit coverage verifies availability gating, submenu selection, and the visible/ARIA label.
issues.title: Add Dev Container option to Agents workspace picker folder menu

issues.body:
## Feature request

In the Agents window, after I click the **Commit** or **Sync** button in the title bar, the button disappears. I assume this means the action completed successfully, but there is no clear confirmation of the resulting state of my changes.

## Current behavior

1. Open an agent session with changes ready to commit or sync.
2. Click **Commit** or **Sync** in the title bar.
3. The button disappears without an explicit success confirmation or an indication of the new repository state.

The disappearing button indirectly suggests success, but leaves uncertainty about whether the action completed and what state the changes are now in.

## Suggested behavior

After either action completes, show clear confirmation and the resulting state—for example, a brief success message and/or persistent status indicating that changes are committed, synced, or up to date. Failures should remain clearly distinguishable from successful completion. This doesn't need to be in a modal or anything the user needs to interact with or dismiss, but perhaps inline?
issues.title: Agents window: Show confirmation after Commit and Sync actions complete

The Agents window should provide one clear **Work in Repository** entry point instead of separate cloud and clone actions.

When a user selects a GitHub repository that is not already available as a local folder:

- select it immediately as a cloud workspace without cloning
- default the session harness to Cloud
- continue to support pasted GitHub repository URLs
- show all repositories the user can access, not only repositories where they have push permission

If the user later selects a harness that requires a local workspace:

- ask where the repository should be cloned
- clone it only at that point
- switch to the harness the user selected after cloning completes
- preserve the existing cloud workspace and harness if cloning is cancelled or fails

Pasted non-GitHub Git repository URLs should retain the existing clone fallback because they cannot be represented as GitHub cloud workspaces.

The workspace picker should also distinguish repository entries from folders with an unlabeled divider while keeping local Git checkouts in the folder section.
issues.title: Agents: use a cloud-first repository selection workflow

When an agent session's pull requests have merged, the archive/mark-as-done suggestion is the moment users are already deciding how to clean up finished work. The automatic cleanup settings added in #334341 are currently discoverable only through Settings or the separate one-time notification, so users cannot configure future cleanup directly from this contextual suggestion.

Add a **Configure Automatic Cleanup** action to the merged-PR archive/mark-as-done suggestion. The action should open Settings filtered to both:

- `chat.agentSessions.autoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays`
- `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays`

The action should only open Settings and must not implicitly enable permanent deletion. It should remain secondary to the immediate Archive/Mark as Done action, wrap cleanly at narrow widths, participate in normal keyboard navigation, be disabled while archiving is in progress, and be included in accessibility help.
issues.title: Expose automatic cleanup settings in the merged-PR archive suggestion

**Summary**

The Agents window (Preview) title bar intentionally does not render the `window.title` setting. This is explicit in the source code:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/titlebarPart.ts

```ts
private _windowTitle: WindowTitle | undefined;

get windowTitle(): WindowTitle {
	// The Agents window title bar does not render `window.title`, so we
	// lazily construct a `WindowTitle` only when a consumer (e.g. a custom
	// command center widget) actually asks for one.
	if (!this._windowTitle) {
```

By contrast, `workbench.colorCustomizations` tokens for the Agents window shell *are* themeable via `agents.background` / `agentsPanel.foreground` (`src/vs/sessions/common/theme.ts`), so background theming works fine, but the title text does not follow the user's `window.title` template.

**Motivation / use case**

Users who run multiple VS Code profiles/instances for different contexts (e.g. a "private" instance vs. a "work" instance, using separate `--user-data-dir`s) commonly customize `window.title` (e.g. prefixing with an emoji or label like `🔒 PRIVAT — ${activeEditorShort}${separator}${rootName}`) together with `titleBar.activeBackground` colorCustomizations, so it's visually obvious at a glance which instance/profile a window belongs to.

Since the Agents window now supports the background/foreground color tokens (`agents.background`, `agentsPanel.foreground`), it's inconsistent that the same visual-identification mechanism doesn't extend to the title/session-picker text shown in the center `Menus.CommandCenter` toolbar.

**Request**

Please consider either:
1. Honoring `window.title` (or a subset of its variables) for the Agents window's center toolbar text, prefixed/suffixed around the existing session/repo picker, or
2. Introducing a dedicated setting (e.g. `agents.window.title` or similar) that lets users add a custom label/prefix to the Agents window, analogous to how `agents.background` now themes the shell.

This would let users visually distinguish Agents windows across different profiles/instances the same way they already can for regular VS Code windows.

**Environment**

- VS Code version: 1.137.0
- OS: Windows
issues.title: Agents window: support window.title (or equivalent) for the center title bar text

issues.body:
## Summary

The merged-agent-session cleanup settings currently use `0` to disable lifecycle cleanup and only accept positive whole-day thresholds. This prevents users from opting into archival as soon as an inactive session's pull request is merged and makes the cleanup test plan require waiting at least a full day.

## Proposed behavior

- `chat.agentSessions.autoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - `-1`: disabled (default)
  - `0`: archive immediately on the next lifecycle evaluation once all existing eligibility checks pass
  - positive integer: archive after that many inactive days
- `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - `-1`: disabled (default)
  - positive integer: permanently delete after that many days following automatic archival
  - `0` remains invalid so permanent deletion always has a grace period

All existing safeguards remain in effect: active/external sessions are excluded, related pull requests are refreshed and must have no open PR, worktree cleanup fails closed, only automatically archived sessions are deletion-eligible, and lifecycle state is revalidated immediately before side effects.

## Test plan impact

Update #335536 to verify immediate archival with `0`, disabled cleanup with `-1`, and rejection of `0` for permanent deletion.

Related: #334341, #335536
issues.title: Allow immediate automatic archival for merged agent sessions

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Summary

Allow custom editors to target language IDs in addition to filename globs, and allow users to configure a language-wide default editor from **Reopen Editor With...** and the editor-type dropdown in breadcrumbs.

Today, `contributes.customEditors[].selector` only supports `filenamePattern`. This forces custom editors to duplicate every filename association of a language and means they do not automatically apply to extensions or filename patterns added through `files.associations`.

For example, Markdown recognizes many extensions and filename patterns, while the built-in Markdown custom editors currently have to target specific globs such as `*.md`. A file associated with the `markdown` language under a different extension does not offer those custom editors.

Related prior discussion: #129553 established that associating a language with a custom editor is not currently possible, but it was closed as a question and does not track the feature or language-wide default behavior. The selector shape was originally designed for future expansion similar to document selectors: #94384.

## Proposed custom editor selector

Support a `language` field in custom editor selectors:

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "customEditors": [
      {
        "viewType": "example.markdownEditor",
        "displayName": "Markdown Editor",
        "priority": "option",
        "selector": [
          {
            "language": "markdown"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Existing `filenamePattern` selectors must remain supported. If both fields are specified in one selector, they should be combined as an AND condition; entries in the selector array remain OR conditions. This would allow selectors such as:

```json
"selector": [
  {
    "language": "markdown",
    "filenamePattern": "docs/**"
  }
]
```

Language matching should use the resource's effective language ID:

- On initial open, infer it from registered language contributions and `files.associations`.
- If a text model already exists, use its current language ID.
- Re-evaluate editor availability when the model language or language associations change.

This avoids requiring a custom editor to copy a language's extension, filename, and filename-pattern lists.

## Reopen With and breadcrumbs

When a language selector matches, the custom editor should appear consistently in:

- **Reopen Editor With...**
- the editor-type dropdown shown in breadcrumbs
- the **Reopen Editor With** submenu in the editor title overflow menu
- normal editor resolution when the contribution has default priority
- diff editor resolution when the contribution opts into diffs

All these surfaces should use the same resolver match result so they cannot disagree about editor availability.

## Language-wide default editor associations

When an editor is available because of a language selector, choosing **Set Default** should create a language-wide default instead of deriving a glob from the current file's extension.

For example, the UI could show:

> Set Default for 'Markdown'

A possible settings representation is:

```json
"workbench.editorLanguageAssociations": {
  "markdown": "example.markdownEditor"
},
"workbench.diffEditorLanguageAssociations": {
  "markdown": "example.markdownEditor"
}
```

The exact storage shape is an implementation detail, but it should support independent normal-editor and diff-editor defaults, matching the existing `workbench.editorAssociations` and `workbench.diffEditorAssociations` behavior.

Suggested precedence:

1. A matching explicit filename-pattern association
2. A matching explicit language association
3. The natural priority of matching editor contributions
4. The default text editor fallback

Diff-specific associations should take precedence over normal-editor associations in diff views.

This preserves precise filename overrides while allowing one default to cover all resources associated with a language, including custom extensions configured through `files.associations`.

## Expected behavior

Given:

```json
"files.associations": {
  "*.notes": "markdown"
},
"workbench.editorLanguageAssociations": {
  "markdown": "example.markdownEditor"
}
```

and a custom editor with `{ "language": "markdown" }`:

1. Opening `README.md` uses `example.markdownEditor`.
2. Opening `meeting.notes` also uses `example.markdownEditor`.
3. **Reopen Editor With...** and the breadcrumbs editor-type dropdown offer the same editor choices for both files.
4. A more-specific filename association can override the language-wide default for either file.
5. Existing extensions using only `filenamePattern` continue to behave unchanged.
issues.title: Allow custom editors and editor defaults to target language IDs

## Problem

The server currently allows only 50 messages between sessions. Complex multi-session workflows can hit this limit quickly, after which coordination messages are not delivered and the user must manually relay them between sessions.

The resulting message is similar to:

> Coordination limitation: session messaging reached its limit, so neither relay was delivered.

## Scenario

1. Query all CI failures from the last week and ask an agent to classify them.
2. Ask the agent to start sessions to fix the top 6-10 issues.
3. Many fixes have overlapping changes, so the sessions need to coordinate frequently.
4. The 50-message limit is reached before the work is complete, blocking further inter-session coordination.

## Request

Increase the number of server-side messages allowed between sessions from 50 to a meaningfully higher value so coordination-heavy workflows can complete without manual message relaying.

## Verification

1. Set `chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits` to `off` and start a new Agent Host session.
2. Ask the agent to create enough sessions/chats or send enough inter-session messages to reach the legacy limit.
3. Verify the limit is enforced with a clear error and rejected operations leave no partial session or chat.
4. Change the setting to `on` without reloading.
5. Repeat the orchestration workflow and verify the increased process-wide session, chat, and message limits apply live.
6. Verify reaching a limit does not interrupt already-running sessions.
7. Ask the agent to recursively create nested delegated work and verify spawn depth remains capped at three.
8. Toggle the setting back to `off` and verify subsequent operations use the original limits without restarting.

Implemented by #337954.
issues.title: Increase the inter-session messaging limit beyond 50

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) custom models to configure additional request body fields via an `extraBody` property in `chatLanguageModels.json`. This would enable users to pass model-specific parameters that are not currently supported through the existing `modelOptions` configuration.
(**This text was created with Copilot!**)

## Use Case

When using custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints (like vLLM, local inference servers, or specialized APIs), models often require additional parameters beyond the currently supported `temperature` and `top_p`:

- `reasoning_effort` (for reasoning models)
- `preserve_thinking` (to retain internal reasoning in responses)
- `chat_template_kwargs` (for custom chat template configuration)
- Provider-specific parameters for cache control, routing, or session management
- Custom model options (e.g., `output_config`, nested configuration objects)

### Example Configuration

```json
{
  "vendor": "customendpoint",
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3",
      "name": "2xDGX-GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3",
      "url": "http://myAIServer:8600/v1",
      "toolCalling": true,
      "vision": true,
      "maxInputTokens": 262144,
      "maxOutputTokens": 32768,
      "modelOptions": {
        "temperature": 0.2,
        "top_p": 0.95
      },
      "extraBody": {
        "reasoning_effort": "none",
        "preserve_thinking": false,
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "enable_thinking": false
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Current Limitations

1. **Only `temperature` and `top_p` are supported** in `modelOptions` (see `byokProvider.ts` lines 308-321 and `openAIEndpoint.ts` lines 302-324)
2. **No generic body customization** - users cannot pass arbitrary request body fields
3. **Model initialization failures** - models that require additional parameters cannot be properly configured
4. **Inconsistent with other extensions** - some extensions (e.g., Kilo Code) already support custom header and body configuration

## Proposed Solution

### Option A: Flexible `extraBody` Field (Recommended)

Add an optional `extraBody` field to model capabilities that allows arbitrary JSON to be merged into the request body:

```typescript
export interface BYOKModelCapabilities {
  // ... existing fields ...
  /**
   * Additional fields to merge into the request body.
   * These override default values but can be overridden by per-request parameters.
   */
  extraBody?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

**Implementation:**
- Merge `extraBody` into the request body after model options are applied
- Deep merge for nested objects
- Per-request parameters take precedence

### Option B: Explicit Parameter List

Extend `modelOptions` to support common additional parameters:
- `reasoning_effort`
- `preserve_thinking`
- Custom output configuration options

**Pros:** More type-safe, better validation
**Cons:** Less flexible, requires updating schema for each new parameter

## Additional Context

- Related to #316794 (custom headers request)
- Affects users of local deployments (vLLM, ollama, custom inference servers)
- Impacts compatibility with specialized reasoning models (DeepSeek, Claude with thinking)
- See #312746 for related issue with reasoning content handling

## Suggested Implementation Path

1. Add `extraBody?: Record<string, unknown>` to `BYOKModelCapabilities` interface
2. Update JSON schema in `package.json` to allow `extraBody` object
3. Modify `OpenAIEndpoint._applyConfiguredModelOptions()` to merge `extraBody` into request body
4. Ensure per-request parameters still take precedence
5. Add unit tests for body merging behavior
6. Document in language model customization guide

## Related Issues

- #316794 - Support custom headers or stable chat session identifiers for BYOK
- #312746 - Copilot Chat drops reasoning_content field with DeepSeek models
- #319968 - Optional model discovery for customendpoint
- #318748 - Custom endpoint model display issues
issues.title: Feature: Support extraBody configuration for BYOK custom models

When switching between sessions in the Agents Window, the editor layout is currently shared globally across the app instead of being restored per session.

For example, a session that uses a diff may have a split layout with a secondary pane. Switching from that session to a no-workspace, chat-only session preserves the split and leaves half of the window occupied by an empty pane. That pane cannot be used directly without opening something through the Command Palette.

This becomes increasingly disruptive as sessions vary between chat-only work and sessions using terminals, diffs, or browsers.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an agent session and arrange the window so a diff or another resource occupies a separate pane.
2. Switch to a chat-only session, such as a no-workspace session.
3. Observe that the previous session's split layout remains, leaving an empty pane.

## Expected behavior

Each agent session restores its own layout, so chat-only sessions can use the full window while sessions with terminals, diffs, browsers, or other resources retain their own arrangement.

## Actual behavior

The layout is global across sessions, so switching between sessions with different resource needs can leave large empty panes that are not directly useful.

Reported with two screen recordings demonstrating the behavior in Slack.
issues.title: Agents Window layout should be restored per session

## Description

In a long-running Agent Host session in the Agents Window, the resource pills beside the chat input keep accumulating every recorded GitHub issue and pull request. Older entries remain indefinitely, and there is no visible way to remove individual stale references or clear a collection.

In the observed session, the input footer had grown to:

- 15 Pull Requests
- 15 Issues
- 2 Artifacts

As the session continues, these collections become increasingly noisy and make it difficult to find the resources that are relevant to the current work.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start an Agent Host session in the Agents Window.
2. Keep using the same session across multiple tasks involving GitHub issues and pull requests.
3. Record or encounter additional issues and pull requests throughout the session.
4. Observe the resource pills beside the chat input.

## Actual behavior

- Issue and pull-request entries continually accumulate for the lifetime of the session.
- Old or no-longer-relevant references remain mixed with current ones.
- The UI offers no apparent way to remove an individual entry or clear stale references.
- The summary counts continue growing, making the collections less useful over time.

## Expected behavior

Long-running sessions should have a manageable lifecycle for recorded resources. The UI should remain useful as references accumulate, for example by allowing stale entries to be removed or cleared and by avoiding duplicate entries for the same resource.

Explicitly recorded durable artifacts can remain persistent if that is intentional, but ordinary issue and pull-request references should not grow without any user control.

## Related work

- #335383 addressed preserving issue and pull-request titles in these pills.
- #335896 covers rich previews and interaction with the collections.

This report is specifically about retention and unbounded collection growth rather than pill rendering or preview content.
issues.title: Long-running Agent Host sessions accumulate issue and pull-request references without cleanup

issues.body:
## Feature request

Allow an extension-contributed keybinding to inherit the effective keybindings of another command while executing a different command in a different context.

For example:

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "keybindings": [
      {
        "command": "markdown.editor.moveLinesUp",
        "inheritFrom": {
          "command": "editor.action.moveLinesUpAction",
          "when": "editorTextFocus && !editorReadonly"
        },
        "when": "markdownEditorTextFocus && markdownEditorWritable"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Motivation

Alternative editors can implement the same editing operation as the code editor but need a different command because their implementation and focus context differ. Today they must copy the code editor's physical default keybindings into their own extension manifest.

This has two problems:

- User customizations of the code editor command do not apply to the alternative editor command.
- Platform-specific defaults, secondary bindings, chords, arguments, and future changes must be duplicated and kept synchronized.

The experimental Markdown editor is a concrete example. It has host-routable `markdown.editor.*` commands and a generated copy of the corresponding keybindings. It should be possible for one customized keybinding to apply to both the code editor and Markdown editor while each retains its own command implementation.

Related: microsoft/vscode-packages#292 and #329414.

## Proposed semantics

A keybinding rule is currently resolved approximately as:

```text
keybinding + context -> command + args
```

Inheritance would project the effective bindings in the other direction:

```text
source command + source context -> keybinding rules + args
```

and then create target rules:

```text
inherited keybinding + target context -> target command + inherited args
```

`inheritFrom.when` identifies the source command's relevant keybinding family. This is necessary because one command can have multiple bindings with different context expressions and arguments. The outer `when` controls where the projected target bindings apply.

The projection should include all matching effective source bindings rather than selecting only one preferred binding. This includes primary and secondary bindings, chords, platform-specific variants, and user-added bindings.

### Arguments

Inherited bindings should preserve their source `args` by default. This is important for commands where multiple keybindings target one command ID and arguments distinguish the operation.

An explicit outer `args` could replace the inherited arguments:

```json
{
  "command": "markdown.editor.move",
  "inheritFrom": {
    "command": "coreEditor.move",
    "when": "editorTextFocus"
  },
  "args": {
    "direction": "up",
    "by": "logicalMarkdownLine"
  },
  "when": "markdownEditorTextFocus"
}
```

Initial semantics should replace arguments rather than deep-merge them.

### User customizations

The expected ordering is:

```text
source defaults
+ source user bindings
- source removals
-> inherited projection
+ explicit target bindings
- target removals
```

Therefore:

- Rebinding the source command also rebinds the target command.
- Removing a source binding removes its inherited projection.
- Users can still add or remove target-only bindings.
- Explicit target bindings take precedence over inherited ones.

## Additional considerations

- Detect and reject inheritance cycles.
- Preserve the source binding's arguments and provenance.
- Expose inherited bindings in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor, including the source command.
- Recompute projections when user keybindings or extension keybindings change.
- Keep command identity and execution separate: invoking the source command programmatically should not invoke the target command.
- Consider whether a future context-key mapping form is needed to preserve residual source conditions instead of replacing the source `when` entirely.
issues.title: Allow extension keybindings to inherit from another command

issues.body:
### Summary

Transition GitHub and Microsoft authentication used by agents to the host-owned authentication model proposed in [microsoft/agent-host-protocol#404](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/404).

### Current architecture

VS Code owns the authentication state and obtains credentials through its authentication providers, then brokers tokens to the agent host. This couples agent authentication to the VS Code client and extension host lifecycle.

### Desired architecture

- The agent host/runtime owns its GitHub and Microsoft account state and credentials.
- VS Code no longer retains authentication state solely to pass tokens into the agent host.
- When an interactive authentication flow is required, the host delegates client-specific UI operations such as opening a browser to VS Code through the Agent Host Protocol.
- Authentication state and flows follow the host-owned auth proposal while preserving an appropriate client-brokered path for sandboxed hosts.

### Scope

Focus initially on GitHub and Microsoft authentication, including account discovery, sign-in, sign-out, token refresh, and migration from the existing VS Code-owned token flow.
issues.title: Transition GitHub and Microsoft authentication to host-owned auth

### Problem

When the voice backend rejects a confirmation narration with a `narration_ack` disposition of `invalid`, the client drops the narration and emits `voiceNarrationDropped` with `kind: 'confirmation'` and `reason: 'invalid'`. This identifies the outcome, but not why the backend rejected the request, making it difficult to diagnose confirmations that are not spoken.

`IVoiceNarrationAck` already includes an optional backend `reason`. `_handleNarrationAck` writes it to the local trace log but does not include a diagnostic category in telemetry.

### Proposed change

Preserve the existing `reason` field as the disposition/drop category, and add a separate bounded, categorized rejection-reason field to `voiceNarrationDropped` for invalid confirmation narrations.

- Define an allowlisted set of stable reason codes based on the backend contract. Coordinate a typed backend reason code if the current reason is free-form.
- Map missing or unrecognized reasons to explicit `missing`/`unknown` categories.
- Do not forward raw backend reason text, narration text, transcripts, session descriptions, or identifiers into the new field.
- Add the appropriate telemetry classification and document the new field's semantics.
- Preserve existing narration drop/retry behavior.

### Relevant code

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/voiceClient/voiceClientService.ts`: `IVoiceNarrationAck.reason`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/voiceClient/voiceSessionController.ts`: `_handleNarrationAck`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/voiceClient/voiceTelemetry.ts`: `VoiceNarrationDroppedEvent` and `VoiceNarrationDroppedClassification`

### Acceptance criteria

- Invalid confirmation narration events distinguish known rejection causes while retaining `kind: 'confirmation'` and `reason: 'invalid'`.
- Missing/unrecognized backend reasons do not leak free-form content.
- Focused tests cover known, missing, and unrecognized reasons, and verify that accepted/busy acknowledgements retain their existing behavior.

cc @meganrogge
issues.title: Voice Mode: record a categorized rejection reason for invalid confirmation narrations

issues.body:
When an orchestrating agent creates a session for read-only research, the session is still created with a new worktree even when the agent omits the `worktree` option. This is surprising because the agent interprets omission as opting out of worktree creation.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Ask an agent to create a child/session for a read-only research task.
2. Have the agent omit the `worktree` option because no code changes are expected.
3. Observe that the session is created in a new worktree anyway.

## Expected behavior

The session creation API should provide a clear, explicit way for an orchestrating agent to create a session in the current workspace without allocating a new worktree. The tool schema/documentation should also make the default behavior unambiguous so agents do not assume omission disables worktree creation.

## Actual behavior

Omitting `worktree` still creates a new worktree, causing unnecessary worktrees for research-only questions.
issues.title: Allow agents to create research sessions without a new worktree

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
## Summary

Expose the focused Explorer item's symlink status as a when-clause context key, so extensions can contribute Explorer context-menu items that appear only when the selected file or folder is a symbolic link.

Suggested name: `explorerResourceIsSymbolicLink` (boolean), consistent with the existing `explorerResourceIsFolder`, `explorerResourceIsRoot`, and `explorerResourceReadonly` keys.

## Problem

There is no way to conditionally show an `explorer/context` menu item for symlinks. Extensions that add symlink-specific commands (for example "Go to symlink target", "Copy real path", or "Reveal original") must currently show the menu item for every file and folder, and reject non-symlinks inside the command handler with an error message.

Concretely:

1. The Explorer already tracks this state internally. `ExplorerItem.isSymbolicLink` is set when resolving the file stat, and is used by core code (for example, `fileActions.ts` skips delete confirmation for symlinks).
2. That state is never bound to a context key. `ExplorerView.setContextKeys()` binds folder, readonly, root, and editor-availability contexts, but not symlink status. The `ResourceContextKey` class likewise exposes scheme, filename, path, and language, but nothing about symlinks.
3. The documented workaround does not work for this case. The suggested pattern is to compute the state in an extension and publish it via the `setContext` command. But an extension receives no event between the user's right-click and menu evaluation, so it cannot know which tree element is about to be menu-scoped. There is no supported way to set a per-item context key in time.

The result is that every user of a symlink extension sees a context-menu entry on all files, and gets an "this is not a symbolic link" notification when they misuse it. The feature is common enough that macOS Finder ships a built-in equivalent ("Show Original").

## Requested behavior

- When the focused Explorer item is a symlink: `explorerResourceIsSymbolicLink` is `true`.
- Otherwise, it is `false` (or unset).
- The key follows the existing pattern for Explorer resource context keys: it updates when the selection or context-menu target changes, and it is usable from `package.json` menu contributions and keybinding `when` clauses.

Example contribution this would enable:

```json
"menus": {
  "explorer/context": [
    {
      "command": "myExt.goToSymlinkSource",
      "when": "explorerResourceIsSymbolicLink",
      "group": "navigation"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Implementation notes

The data already exists per Explorer item at the moment context keys are set, so this looks like a small change:

- In `ExplorerView.setContextKeys(stat)`, bind the new key alongside the existing ones (approximately one added `IContextKey` plus one `set()` call).
- Register the key in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/common/files.ts` next to the other `RawContextKey` declarations, so it appears in the `when-clause-contexts` documentation.
- Multi-root/remote caveats apply as they do for the other resource context keys: the value reflects the item under focus, including across multi-workspace trees and remote file system providers.
- No new API surface in `vscode.d.ts` is required, so no engine-version bump for consumers.

## Related

- #167996 — asked for a when-clause check for symlinks (closed as out-of-scope, but the suggested `setContext` workaround cannot work, as explained in the issue thread itself).
- #179307 — asked for a built-in "Reveal Symbolic Link Original" Explorer menu item; same root cause.
- #159722 — users expect symlink indication in the Explorer (the arrow decoration); the context key request is the menu/when-clause counterpart.
issues.title: Feature Request: expose an `explorerResourceIsSymbolicLink` context key for when clauses

issues.body:
When a trusted workspace declares a marketplace and plugin in `.github/copilot/settings.json`, Copilot CLI treats `enabledPlugins` as a repository-scoped activation overlay: `true` installs/enables the plugin for that repository, and the plugin is not enabled globally.

VS Code reads the same file, but currently treats `enabledPlugins: true` only as a recommendation requiring manual installation. This gives the same configuration different semantics across the two clients.

Expected: align VS Code with Copilot CLI for trusted workspaces:

- `true`: ensure the plugin is installed and activate it for the repository.
- `false`: deactivate it for the repository.
- absent: preserve the user/global state.
- Do not persist repository-only enablement into global user settings.
- Ignore repository plugin settings until the workspace is trusted.

The initial workspace-plugin implementation explicitly left enablement/disablement unification as follow-up: #300585.

Related: #327404 tracks a bug in the current recommendation flow; this issue tracks the underlying cross-client behavior alignment.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._
issues.title: Align repository enabledPlugins behavior with Copilot CLI

## Feature request

Please expose a theme color for the connected active editor tab outline in the Modern UI, so users can configure it through `workbench.colorCustomizations` in regular light and dark themes (for example, Light 2026).

The requested outline is the top and sides of the active tab, open at the bottom and joined to the editor surface, as shown in the attached high-contrast screenshot. This is **not** the outer frame around the entire editor area, including all inactive tabs.

## Current behavior

- High-contrast themes already display this connected outline, using `focusBorder` for the active editor group and `contrastBorder` for inactive groups.
- The CSS applying those colors is gated on `.hc-black` / `.hc-light`. In regular light/dark themes, the connected-tab border instead uses the tab surface color and the connected editor-well border is transparent.
- `tab.activeBorder` and `tab.activeBorderTop` do not provide this outline with Modern UI connected tabs.
- `editor.border` colors the outer editor frame, not the requested active-tab outline.

## Desired behavior

Allow users/theme authors to choose a color for this connected tab outline without switching to a high-contrast theme. Ideally, support the corresponding connected editor-pane outline and distinguish active/inactive editor groups, while preserving the current appearance when no color is configured.

Relevant implementation: [connectedEditorTabs.css, lines 14–26](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/browser/media/connectedEditorTabs.css#L14-L26) and [active tab border, lines 160–173](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/browser/media/connectedEditorTabs.css#L160-L173).

The attached screenshot below illustrates the existing high-contrast outline that should be customizable in regular themes.
issues.title: Allow customizing the connected active editor tab outline in light and dark themes

Hi, I wanted to bring this up again because Electron 44 seems to have added support for this now. 

On Linux, using:
```
"window.titleBarStyle": "custom",
"window.controlsStyle": "native"
```
keeps the title bar integrated with VS Code, which is nice, but the minimize/maximize/close buttons still don’t really match the desktop theme. On KDE Plasma with Breeze, they look quite different from the normal Breeze window buttons.

Using:
```
"window.titleBarStyle": "native"
```

does give the real Breeze title bar, but then it becomes a separate bar above VS Code, which is not the same thing.
There were already issues about this before (#229053 and #313854), and I saw that devs said "limitation that Electron has" at the time.

Now Electron 44 added system-themed title bar icons for Linux Window Controls Overlay, including Breeze-specific handling: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/52461

So I was wondering if this could be looked at again once

Enterprise Managed Settings `minVersion` lets enterprise administrators block AI features on outdated VS Code clients until users update. For example, an organization can require a release with newer sandboxing protections.

Chat shows an update notice. The Editor also shows a grey Workspace Trust-style banner so users understand why AI is unavailable even when Chat is closed; other editor features remain usable. The Agents window uses only a blocking overlay, with no redundant banner, because the whole window is unavailable.

Recovery uses VS Code's native update actions when available. If enterprise policy disables built-in updates, the notice directs users to their administrator for an approved update.

Existing enforcement is unchanged. Notices show the installed and required versions when available and clear when the restriction is resolved.

Implementation: #337151.
issues.title: Explain enterprise minVersion restrictions in Chat, the Agents window, and a window-level banner

issues.body:
Terminal text in VS Code looks noticeably softer than the same font in Ghostty and other native terminals on macOS HiDPI. I've heard this from a few people: the integrated terminal reads "dull" next to a standalone terminal at the same font and size.

I dug into it and the difference on macOS is the font antialiasing policy, not resolution. Editor and workbench text get one policy, terminal text on the GPU canvas path gets another, so terminal glyphs read heavier and blurrier.

Proposal: an opt-in `terminal.integrated.fontRendering` setting, `inherit` as the unchanged default and `crisp` as the opt-in mode, scoped to terminal text only so the editor, workbench, terminal theme, font family, size and weight don't change. On Windows and Linux the GPU renderer could request grayscale antialiasing through xterm's existing alpha-capable canvas path.

Comparison on macOS HiDPI, left `crisp`, right current:

It should apply to normal, detached and sticky-scroll terminals, and keep terminal image transparency working.

Upstream: xterm.js doesn't expose a font antialiasing option today, so VS Code has to go through the `allowTransparency` canvas path to get this. A dedicated antialiasing/font-rendering option in xterm.js (WebGL and DOM renderers) would let this be a first-class setting rather than a side effect, and would help every xterm.js embedder, not just VS Code. Until then this stays experimental, since the visible result depends on OS, display scale, font and theme.
issues.title: Terminal: support crisp font rendering on HiDPI displays

The currently selected agent and model are shown only as text, which makes it

issues.body:
## Feature request

Add an opt-in **skip if still running** option for automations. When a trigger fires and a session started by an earlier run of the same automation is still running, skip the new run instead of starting another session.

## Motivation

Scheduled or frequently triggered automations can overlap when a previous session takes longer than the trigger interval. Users should be able to prevent duplicate work and competing changes without having to monitor sessions manually.

## Expected behavior

- Make this configurable per automation; preserve the existing behavior when the option is disabled.
- When enabled, check whether a session from an earlier run of that automation is still running before starting another session.
- If so, skip this occurrence rather than queueing it or cancelling the existing session.
- Show the occurrence as skipped, with the reason that an earlier session is still running.
- Once the previous session has finished, subsequent triggers can start sessions normally.
- Apply the overlap guard atomically so simultaneous triggers cannot both start a session.

The precise definition of "still running" (including sessions waiting for user input or approval) should be documented as part of the design.
issues.title: Automations: optionally skip a run while a previous session is still running

issues.body:
## Feature request

Allow an automation to start by executing a script, before creating an AI session. The script should be able to complete the automation entirely without AI participation, or request that a new AI session be started.

Conceptually, an automation could support an action such as `prompt | script`. A script action would perform deterministic work or checks first and decide whether AI is needed.

## Motivation

Many automations can do useful work with a script alone, or cheaply determine that there is nothing for an agent to do. Starting an AI session for every trigger adds unnecessary cost and noise. Conversely, a script may discover work or encounter a failure for which AI assistance is useful.

## Independent outcomes

Script success/failure and the decision to continue with AI should be independent, supporting all four combinations:

| Script result | Start a new AI session? | Intended behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Success | No | Complete the automation successfully without involving AI. |
| Success | Yes | Start a new AI session with the script's output/context for follow-up work. |
| Failure | No | Report the failed script/run without involving AI. |
| Failure | Yes | Start a new AI session with the failure details for investigation or recovery; retain the script failure in the run history. |

## Expected behavior

- Run the script before creating an AI session, not as a tool invocation inside an already-started AI session.
- Provide an explicit, documented way to request or suppress AI continuation independently of the script's success/failure status.
- When continuation is requested, allow a configured prompt and script output/context to be passed to the new session.
- Preserve script output, errors, and exit status in the automation run history, including runs that never create an AI session.
- Surface invalid or missing control output and script execution errors explicitly, with documented behavior.

## Design question: signaling contract

The exact protocol needs design. A special exit code (for example, `-2`) or a stdout marker such as `no-ai` could express "no AI needed", but a single special status conflates independent concerns, and free-form stdout markers may collide with ordinary output.

Consider a structured result or dedicated control channel that expresses the AI-continuation decision separately from the process exit status. The request is for the four combinations above, not a particular exit code or marker. The design should also define how an AI follow-up affects the overall run status after a failed script.
issues.title: Automations: support script-first actions with optional AI continuation

issues.body:
## Motivation

Fresh worktree-isolated agent sessions currently defer worktree creation until the first send so the prompt can influence branch naming. That prevents the agent runtime and workspace-dependent caches from pre-warming, adding avoidable latency to the first turn.

We should investigate whether worktrees can be provisioned or prepared earlier without sacrificing naming quality, correctness, or cleanup guarantees across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Investigation

Explore a cross-platform design for pre-warming agent worktrees, including:

- When pre-warming can start and which inputs are available before the first prompt.
- Whether to create a provisional worktree/branch and rename it later, reserve a path, or split filesystem preparation from Git worktree creation.
- Coordination with Agent Host/runtime pre-warming so providers do not materialize against a pending or incorrect working directory.
- Cancellation, abandoned composers, restart recovery, stale provisional worktrees, and deterministic cleanup.
- Repository locking and races when multiple sessions pre-warm concurrently.
- Windows path-length, file-locking, antivirus, junction/symlink, and case-sensitivity behavior.
- macOS/Linux filesystem and symlink behavior, permissions, and performance differences.
- Interaction with trust, remote workspaces, multi-root workspaces, submodules, sparse checkout, LFS, and `git.worktreeIncludeFiles`.
- Disk usage and limits for speculative worktrees.

## Measurements

Capture baseline and prototype timings for:

- Composer open to worktree ready.
- First send to provider dispatch.
- First meaningful progress.
- Cancellation and cleanup latency.

Measure representative repositories on Windows, macOS, and Linux, including cold and warm filesystem/cache states.

## Done when

- We have a documented recommendation with platform-specific findings and identified risks.
- A prototype demonstrates the viable lifecycle or proves why pre-warming should remain deferred.
- The proposal defines state transitions, recovery/cleanup behavior, resource limits, and the integration point with provider pre-warming.
- Follow-up implementation work is split into scoped issues as needed.
issues.title: Explore cross-platform pre-warming for agent worktrees

issues.body:
## Motivation

Agents should be able to run a bounded bake-off when a task would benefit from comparing multiple models, providers, agents, or configurations. Today this requires manual orchestration and the results are difficult to compare consistently.

## Proposal

Expose an Agent Host tool that an agent can invoke to run the same task or evaluation prompt against a selected set of candidates and receive a structured comparison.

The tool should support:

- Selecting candidate models/providers/agents and an explicit task or evaluation prompt.
- Running candidates in isolated child sessions so they cannot interfere with the current session or each other.
- Configurable concurrency, timeout, and resource limits.
- Consistent result capture, including outcome, summary, changed files/diff, validation results, duration, and available usage/cost signals.
- A structured response that lets the calling agent compare results, explain tradeoffs, and optionally recommend or adopt a winner.
- Cancellation and reliable cleanup of child sessions/worktrees.
- Clear handling for unavailable providers, partial failures, and candidates that require different capabilities.

## Questions to explore

- What should the stable tool schema and result format be?
- Which candidate dimensions should be supported initially: model, provider, custom agent, permission profile, or prompt variation?
- How should success criteria be supplied and evaluated without allowing the judge to silently change the task?
- Which telemetry and user-visible progress are needed?
- What confirmation or policy gates are required before spawning multiple sessions or consuming significant resources?

## Done when

- An agent can invoke the tool with a bounded candidate set.
- Candidate runs are isolated, cancellable, and cleaned up.
- The caller receives comparable structured results and can identify the selected result.
- Tests cover success, partial failure, cancellation, limits, and cleanup.
issues.title: Make agent bake-offs available as an agent-invokable tool

## Feature request

Revamp the Agent Bake Off UI across the full comparison workflow: setup, in-progress attempts, Judge results, and custom synthesis.

## Problem

The current experience is functional, but the UI has grown organically and feels dense and inconsistent across stages. In particular:

- attempt identity, status, and outcome presentation shift between setup, the Sessions list, and the Judge result;
- primary actions compete with secondary actions instead of presenting a clear next step;
- the custom synthesis decision matrix becomes difficult to scan as attempts and decisions increase;
- narrow layouts can force awkward two-dimensional scrolling, wrapping, and clipped controls;
- overflow chrome must consistently use themed workbench scrollables rather than browser-native scrollbars;
- the visual hierarchy does not yet make the recommended attempt, supporting evidence, and synthesis choices feel like one coherent workflow.

## Proposed direction

Design a cohesive Agent Bake Off experience that:

1. Establishes a consistent visual identity for each attempt across setup, progress, results, and synthesis.
2. Gives each stage one clear primary action while keeping alternate actions discoverable but visually secondary.
3. Makes Judge rationale, validation evidence, strengths, timing, and token usage easy to scan and compare.
4. Reworks custom synthesis so decisions remain understandable with multiple attempts and at narrow widths, without clipped content or native scrollbars.
5. Uses standard VS Code controls, themed scrollables, spacing/type roles, focus treatment, and high-contrast behavior.
6. Preserves complete keyboard operation, screen-reader semantics, accessible-view content, and responsive phone behavior.

## Definition of done

- An approved UX proposal covers the end-to-end Bake Off workflow.
- Desktop, narrow-window, and phone layouts are specified.
- Attempt status and action hierarchy are consistent across surfaces.
- Custom synthesis scales to additional attempts and decisions without inaccessible or native overflow UI.
- Implementation includes focused component/unit coverage and visual fixtures for the key states.

Related implementation context: #335498.
issues.title: Revamp the Agent Bake Off comparison UI

## Summary

Add an explicit environment picker to the Agents Window new-session experience. Initially, the picker could offer **Local** and **Remote**, **Cloud** while being designed to accommodate additional environment types over time.

## Motivation

The place where work runs is a distinct choice from the source or workspace being used. Today these concepts can become coupled, making it harder to understand or extend session creation as more execution environments become available.

An environment picker would make this choice visible and establish a scalable model for environments such as:

- **Local** — run on the current machine.
- **Remote** — run through a supported remote connection or host.
- Future environments, such as cloud-hosted, containerized, or other provider-backed environments.

## Proposed direction

- Add an **Environment** picker to the new-session UI.
- Keep environment selection independent from:
  - Source/workspace selection.
  - Agent or harness selection.
  - Session intent.
- Start with **Local** and **Remote** where supported.
- Allow environment providers to contribute availability, display information, configuration/connection actions, and capability constraints without redesigning the picker for every new environment type.
- Remember the user's explicit selection when appropriate.
- Clearly communicate unavailable or unsupported source/environment/harness combinations rather than silently switching environments.
- Ensure the selected environment remains visible before launch and is represented consistently when restoring or inspecting a session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can explicitly choose between available Local and Remote environments when creating a session.
- [ ] Environment selection is modeled separately from the selected source/workspace and agent/harness.
- [ ] The picker can accommodate additional environment types without introducing environment-specific top-level UI.
- [ ] Unsupported combinations are disabled or explained with actionable guidance.
- [ ] The selected environment is preserved across session creation and restoration where applicable.
- [ ] The picker has appropriate keyboard and screen-reader support.

Related to #334563, which identifies independent environment selection as part of the broader workspace picker direction.
issues.title: Agents Window: Add an extensible environment picker

issues.body:
### Feature request

The BYOK "custom endpoint" model configuration (`vendor: "customendpoint"`) only accepts a **static** credential in `apiKey` (or `requestHeaders`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`. There is no way to supply a **dynamically generated / short-lived** token.

This blocks any enterprise gateway that uses **OAuth** instead of static API keys, because OAuth access tokens are short-lived (e.g. ~1h) and must be refreshed. Today the only options are (a) manually pasting a fresh token every hour, or (b) running a local reverse-proxy that injects the token — both are poor workarounds for what should be first-class.

### Requested behavior

Add a way for the custom endpoint to obtain its credential dynamically per request, e.g.:

- An `apiKeyHelper`-style setting pointing to a local script/command whose stdout is the current token (same model as Claude Code's [`apiKeyHelper`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#credential-management)), and/or
- Support for `${env:VAR}` / secret references resolved at request time in `apiKey` / `requestHeaders`.

### Concrete use case

Authenticating against a **Databricks AI Gateway** (`/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`) with OAuth (U2M) instead of a personal access token. The Databricks CLI already mints and auto-refreshes OAuth tokens (`databricks auth token`); an `apiKeyHelper` hook would let it feed the current token to VS Code transparently.

### Prior issues

This was previously requested and closed **not planned** — #318762 (closed only for lack of 20 upvotes, not on technical grounds) and #322499 (dynamic Bearer token, incl. the Databricks AI Gateway scenario). Re-filing since demand persists.

### Environment

- VS Code Version: 1.139.0
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.1 (25G76)
- Extension: GitHub Copilot Chat (BYOK / Manage Models)

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A (feature request)
issues.title: BYOK custom endpoints: support dynamic/refreshable API key (apiKeyHelper) for OAuth-based gateways
