Release notes and documentation can explain a feature, but users still have to leave the content, find the relevant UI, and reconstruct the example themselves. This makes newly announced or unfamiliar functionality harder to discover and evaluate.

VS Code should support trusted **Try This** links that connect release notes and documentation to locally registered product experiences. Depending on the feature, an example could:

- open an existing view or command;
- prepare an isolated, read-only sample;
- open the relevant UI and guide the user through its controls;
- explain missing prerequisites and offer an explicit setup action; or
- hand off to the correct VS Code window, including the Agents window.

The fetched Markdown should contain only a stable tryout identifier. Installed VS Code code should own all titles, descriptions, commands, arguments, samples, availability checks, and guided steps. Unknown, malformed, unavailable, or stale identifiers should remain inert.

The experience should preserve normal product safeguards and accessibility. It must not automatically trust a workspace, enable settings, install extensions, accept confirmations, select a model or provider, submit Chat input, or modify user resources. External documentation links should require confirmation before launching an installed example.

Reference implementation: #337713
issues.title: Support trusted “Try This” experiences in release notes and documentation

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
### Feature Description

Following the implementation of milestone **1.126.0** (Issue #317977), VS Code introduced excellent per-message token usage and cost metrics badges. However, this telemetry metric framework is currently tightly coupled to internal GitHub Copilot billing schemas. 

As the **VS Code Agents** environment scales to allow developers to bring their own model endpoints and provider-agnostic infrastructure, there is currently no way to bubble up per-session cost tracking from third-party AI gateways like **Vercel AI Gateway**. Alternative tools like OpenCode already process this by default by remaining completely provider-agnostic while still tracking session spend.

When routing model traffic through a custom gateway, providers inject metadata headers directly into the stream payload (for instance, Vercel’s `x-vercel-ai-gateway-spend` or standard token counters). VS Code currently strips or discards these custom header footprints from the UI layer.

### Proposed Solution

1. **Expose an Extensible Metadata Parser Hook:** Allow the core chat and agent UI components to intercept response headers from the active language model provider stream.
2. **Support Dynamic Cost Badge Mapping:** Introduce a configuration setting or API hook where users or extensions can map arbitrary header keys (like `x-vercel-ai-gateway-spend` or custom token parameters) directly into the native UI session badge footer.
3. **Preserve Session Mapping:** Ensure that `chatSessionResource` contexts pass downstream response parameters accurately so extensions can reliably track session budgets without requiring brittle, backward-scanning hacks.

### Alternative Solutions Considered

- Using third-party extensions, but these cannot cleanly hook into the newly implemented native agent/chat session footer badges because the core framework discards custom provider telemetry headers.
- Constantly running `vercel ai-gateway api-keys inspect` in a side terminal, which breaks the flow of development inside the agent workspace.

### Additional Context

Giving developers real-time feedback on their chosen agnostic gateway's spending directly inside the active editor pane ensures proper budget boundaries and model optimization during long multi-agent loops.

Ref: #317977
issues.title: [Feature Request] Display token and cost consumption of external Gateways (e.g., Vercel AI Gateway)

VS Code Version: 1.139.1 (system setup)
OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19045

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Split the editor into three side-by-side editor groups.
2. Click any editor group to focus it.

Actual Result:
The clicked editor group automatically expands and occupies more space, while the other two groups shrink.

Expected Result:
All editor groups maintain fixed widths. Focusing a group by clicking should not trigger any resizing of editor panels.

I have searched all settings but cannot find an option to disable this auto-resize behavior.
issues.title: Disable automatic expansion of editor group on click

issues.body:
## Feature request

Support product-protocol links that open the Agents Window **New Session** composer with a workspace selected and an unsent prompt populated.

Proposed URL shape:

```text
vscode-insiders://agents/new?workspace=<encoded-workspace-uri>&prompt=<encoded-prompt>
```

For example:

```sh
open "vscode-insiders://agents/new?workspace=file%3A%2F%2F%2FUsers%2Fsandy081%2Fwork%2Fvscode&prompt=Explain%20how%20this%20project%20runs%20its%20tests.%20Do%20not%20run%20anything%20yet."
```

Opening the link should:

1. Open or focus the Agents Window.
2. Open the **New Session** composer.
3. Select `/Users/sandy081/work/vscode` as the workspace.
4. Populate this prompt without submitting it:

   > Explain how this project runs its tests. Do not run anything yet.

The prompt must remain an editable draft so the user can review or change it before sending.

An initial implementation was attempted in #337360.
issues.title: Agents Window: Populate New Session drafts from product protocol links

Allow an independent Agent Host session to be created without a workspace, even when the source session is workspace-backed.

Verification:
1. Open a workspace-backed Agent Host session.
2. Ask the agent: `Create a new independent session without a workspace. Ask it to reply with workspaceless session ready.`
3. Open the created session and verify it has no selected workspace or repository.
4. Verify it did not inherit the source session folder.
5. Verify the request was delivered and the session responds.
6. Reload the Agents Window and verify the workspaceless session still appears and opens.

Implemented by #337230.
issues.title: Agent Host: Verify workspaceless independent session creation

issues.body:
Verify the experimental `chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits` setting and its live process-wide limits for agent-created sessions, chats, and messages.

Verification:
1. Set `chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits` to `off` and start a new Agent Host session.
2. Ask the agent to create enough sessions/chats or send enough messages to approach the legacy limit.
3. Verify the legacy limit is enforced with a clear error and rejected operations leave no partial session or chat.
4. Change the setting to `on` without reloading.
5. Repeat the orchestration workflow and verify the increased process-wide session, chat, and message limits apply live.
6. Verify ordinary permissions, confirmations, and input validation are unchanged.
7. Ask the agent to recursively create nested delegated work and verify spawn depth remains capped at three.
8. Toggle the setting back to `off` and verify subsequent operations use the original limits without restarting.
9. Exercise the limit from multiple active sessions and verify it is process-wide rather than scoped to one chat.
10. Verify reaching a limit does not interrupt already-running sessions.

Implemented by #337954.
issues.title: Agent Host: Verify configurable orchestration limits

It is already a distinct, agent-first, cross-workspace surface, but currently gets grouped together with all project windows, which makes it inconvenient to switch to when several VS Code windows are open.

issues.body:
When the GitHub Pull Requests extension is installed, clicking a GitHub pull request link in the Agents Window opens the pull request in the extension's PR editor view. There does not appear to be a way to open that link in the external browser instead.

Shift+click and the link context menu still route to the PR editor.

It would be useful to offer an explicit **Open in Browser** action (for example in the link context menu and/or via a modifier click) so users can bypass the extension's link handling when needed.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install/enable the GitHub Pull Requests extension.
2. Open an Agents Window conversation containing a link to a GitHub pull request.
3. Click the link, Shift+click it, or use the link context menu.

### Actual
The pull request opens in the GitHub Pull Requests extension PR editor view.

### Expected
There is an action to force the link to open in the external browser.
issues.title: Allow GitHub pull request links in Agents Window to open in external browser

issues.body:
The new-session composer should keep the primary task focused while making advanced session choices easy to discover and review.

## Feature request

Group secondary new-session controls—such as repository, harness, mode, permissions, model, and other provider-specific options—behind a single progressive-disclosure control. When collapsed, summarize only meaningful non-default effective choices so users can understand consequential state without scanning a row of controls.

The experience should:

- preserve the existing composer layout unless the experimental layout is enabled
- remember expanded/collapsed state and applicable repository-scoped choices
- present the collapsed disclosure as one focus stop with one accessible name
- use standard toolbar and picker keyboard behavior
- support provider-neutral summaries so shared Sessions UI does not depend on individual Agent Host implementations
- remain usable in narrow layouts, high-contrast themes, and with screen readers
- avoid presenting immutable provider state as an interactive choice

Implementation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338465
issues.title: Progressively disclose advanced new-session options in the Agents window
